newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: WE HAVE NOTHING TO HIDE, COMMUNISTS SAY IN SPY ROW.
newsitem.headline: WE HAVE NOTHING TO HIDE, COMMUNISTS SAY IN SPY ROW.

text.p: The unreconstructed Czech Communists joined a pre-election espionage row on Thursday, saying anybody who spied on their party would only discover how clean and open it was.
"If somebody spies on me... even the government coalition will find out that we are a transparent party," said Communist chairman Miroslav Grebenicek.
His party is the direct successor to the secretive organisation which ruled with more than a little help from the now disbanded StB secret police for 41 years until 1989.
The affair began last Friday, a week before Senate polls, when Agriculture Minister Josef Lux alleged the BIS secret service had spied on him three years ago and covered it up.

Acting BIS director Stanislav Devaty, a protege of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, resigned on Monday over the scandal. But he denied that the BIS, which replaced the StB after the fall of communism, had shadowed Lux.

Grebenicek, speaking at a party news conference, blasted the whole government for intentional lack of control of BIS. Devaty was a member of Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) although he suspended his membership when he became spymaster.
The Communists, who won 10.3 percent of the vote in June lower house elections, has gone through virtually no reform since it was ousted from power in 1989.
